steps: Check existing profiles / VLAN and service-port
Create/choose bandwidth-profile, line-profile, ONU profile, service-profile (according to DmOS manual)
Preview service VLAN and service-port graph
Bind ONU per discovered serial on exact GPON interface
Use vendor transactional commit only after reviewed diff
Read back ONU, service-port, PPPoE and optical info
restrictions: Do not issue commit in discovery step

steps: Read show card and show gpon onu uncfg
Select ONU type capabilities (T-CONT/GEM/UNI)
Create TCONT+VLAN+service profiles for firmware
Preview interface gpon-olt_{shelf}/{slot}/{port} ONU authorization
Validate ONU optical state and flows
restrictions: Example ONU110B is not universal to all ONUs
Do not use C3xx syntax on C6xx without validation

steps: Read existing DBA/VLAN profiles
Define or reuse LINE profile with T-CONT, GEM and VLAN mapping
Choose ETH for bridge or VEIP for router
Check compatibility notes for third-party ONU
Preview reference graph and validate ONU capabilities
restrictions: Examples assume DBA 1 and VLAN 1 already exist; do not blindly create

steps: Read flow and bandwidth profiles
Inspect usages to prevent deleting shared profiles
Create service intent then translate to bandwidth/flow/VLAN profiles
Preview ONU binding and test optical state
Verify post-change and backup
restrictions: Never delete a profile while referenced by other ONUs
Apply config via approved engine only

steps: Reuse current DBA/service/line templates from Profile Studio 2.5
Check ONU Run/Config/Match from display ont info
Do not overwrite existing profile IDs
Save and verify through existing executor
restrictions: Do not replace the already implemented Huawei path

steps: Acquire firmware-exact official config docs or export from vendor EMS
Record protocol/CLI and sanitize live output in lab
Create typed profile translation based on verified steps
Add golden fixtures and negative tests before enabling write
restrictions: No write commands available as pre-certified
